chunk-001:c009.proposition: Evolution's immense, inefficient, and frequently biologically or morally useless suffering is significant evidence against a perfectly good providential creator.

orphanFallback.rationale: The proposition independently advances an evidential argument from evolutionary suffering against providential goodness and does not require an earlier opposing move.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-01.proposition: A purely actual God lacks potentialities and contingencies, cannot have done otherwise, and therefore cannot possess the perfect freedom affirmed by traditional theism.

orphanFallback.rationale: The proposition independently alleges an inconsistency between pure actuality and perfect divine freedom, so it remains a complete constructive objection without an earlier opponent move.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-02.proposition: Real temporal change requires God's knowledge to acquire and lose truths, contradicting the immutability and absence of potency asserted by classical theism.

orphanFallback.rationale: The proposition directly presents the changing-knowledge argument from temporal reality and classical immutability, independently of any earlier selected response target.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-05.proposition: Perfect divine love would keep every finite person able to enter a loving relationship with God, making nonresistant unbelief evidence against perfect divine goodness.

orphanFallback.rationale: Even without the earlier claim about unequal epistemic access, the stated connection among perfect love, relationship-enabling belief, and nonresistant unbelief supplies an independent hiddenness argument.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-06.proposition: The first three Thomistic ways commit a quantifier-shift error because each causal chain having a first cause does not entail one shared first cause of every chain.

orphanFallback.rationale: The counselor analogy and per-chain versus common-cause distinction constitute a freestanding logical objection to inferring one universal first cause from separately terminating causal chains.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-08.proposition: The Thomistic causal arguments do not establish a perfectly good or worship-worthy being, so further argument is required to bridge from a first cause to God.

orphanFallback.rationale: The proposition independently identifies a burden-relevant gap between a causal terminus and the morally perfect, worship-worthy deity required by classical theism.

chunk-004:c004-02.proposition: The changing-knowledge argument does not require presentism because propositions vary in truth across temporal locations even under eternalism or growing-block theories.

orphanFallback.rationale: Without an earlier objection about presentism, the proposition still constructively broadens the changing-knowledge case by grounding it in temporally varying truth across several theories of time.

chunk-004:c004-07.proposition: Soul-building and redemptive accounts do not answer evolutionary evil because nonhuman animals endured immense gratuitous pain and little flourishing before moral agents existed.

orphanFallback.rationale: The prehistoric scale and nonmoral subjects of animal suffering independently limit person-centered theodicies, even if no earlier selected move expressly advances those theodicies.

chunk-005:c005-04.proposition: Widespread incompatible religious traditions are surprising if a perfectly loving God exists, making religious disagreement a stronger objection than surface parallels among religions.

orphanFallback.rationale: The mismatch between widespread incompatible traditions and the access expected from perfect divine love supplies an independent evidential argument from religious diversity.
